title: Sustained-degradation staffing and customer communications playbook
author: Nora Patel
content:
Summary:
This playbook prescribes how Redwood responds to sustained degradations (incidents > 4 hours with partial or region-scoped customer impact). It combines an operational staffing model, step-by-step runbook actions for responders and bridge operators, templated status page payloads and customer messages that are safe for legal/security review, and a post-incident learning flow. Use this for multi-hour degradations that require controlled rotations, fatigue mitigation, and structured customer comms across tiers.

Scope and applicability:
- Applies to any incident classified as Sustained Degradation (see classification table below).
- Not for total outage (major incident) — use the Major Incident Runbook.
- Use with service-specific runbooks (link to service runbook in team wiki) and SRE on-call staffing sheets.

Definition and classification (quick table):
| Severity | Impact window | Example signals | Use this playbook when... |
|---------|---------------|----------------|---------------------------|
| Sustained Degradation | >4 hours | Elevated error rate, CPU KV-cache miss growth, regional latency SLO droops | Impact affects some customers or routes persistently and recovery is slow or partial |

Ownership and roles: (Who does what)
- Bridge Operator (primary): run the incident bridge, coordinate comm cadence, maintain the timeline. Typically eng-sre on-call.
- Triage Lead (1st responder): owns triage, implements quick mitigations, pushes changes through canary if required.
- Engineering Pods (service owners): own fixes, PRs, tests. Provide hourly technical updates.
- Capacity & Routing Lead: monitors autoscaling, evictions, rate-limiting and routing fallbacks.
- Customer Success Liaison: prepares customer-impact lists and drafts external comms with legal review.
- Wellbeing & Rotation Coordinator: enforces rest cycles, triages shift replacements after 4+ hours.

Initial activation checklist (first 30 minutes):
1. Bridge Operator: open incident bridge, set title: "Sustained Degradation — <service> — <region>".
2. Triage Lead: collect signals, map to hypotheses, and record top 3 likely causes in bridge notes.
3. Bridge Operator: set initial public status: "Investigating" using the template below.
4. Engineering Pods: start focused debugging; capture reproducible steps.
5. Wellbeing Coordinator: confirm minimum responder coverage for next 8h, designate off-shift backups.

Sustained staffing model (rotations and rest):
- Goal: avoid responder burnout and preserve mental bandwidth for complex remediation.
- Core principle: 3-hour active blocks for engineering leads during sustained incidents, with handoff windows and mandatory 30–45 minute breaks after two blocks.
- Staffing matrix (example):
| Role | Active shift | Relief shift | Max continuous time |
| Bridge Operator | 0–8h (split 2 persons) | 2nd operator queued at 4h | 4h |
| Triage Lead | 0–3h | backup steps in at 3h | 3h |
| Engineering Pod A Lead | 0–3h | handoff to Pod A secondary | 3h |
| Wellbeing Coordinator | continuous monitoring | rotate per 8h schedule | N/A |

Handoff protocol (clean, fast, low-friction):
1. Outgoing responder writes a 2-line summary: current hypothesis, recent actions, top 3 next steps.
2. Run a 5-minute verbal sync with incoming responder on the bridge.
3. Incoming responder confirms they understand and writes acceptance note with timestamp.
4. Bridge Operator updates the timeline and public status if needed.

Technical mitigation runbook (example actions for latency/traffic degradation):
1. Confirm scope with metrics: region, model, route, tenant.
2. If KV cache growth suspected, toggle temporary cache-eviction policy (non-disruptive tiered eviction).
3. If autoscaling not responsive, apply emergency scale-up on dedicated pools for affected region; inform Capacity Lead.
4. Consider immediate, reversible routing policy: shift low-priority traffic to degraded model variant to preserve critical path.
5. If change is deployed, run targeted smoke tests and monitor SLO delta for 5 minutes.

Status page payload templates (public):
- Use concise, plain language. Avoid root-cause speculation. Provide impact, scope, mitigation, and ETA where possible.
1) Investigating initial post (short):
"title: Investigating elevated latency for text-generation in us-west-2
status: investigating
impact: Some customers may experience slower response times and intermittent errors for text-generation requests routed to us-west-2.
scope: A subset of requests for the text-generation API in the US-West region are affected.
mitigation: Engineers are actively investigating. No action required from customers.
updated_at: <ISO8601 timestamp>"

2) Mitigation in progress (when a rollback/scale is in flight):
"title: Mitigation in progress — throttling and routing adjustments
status: identifying a mitigation
impact: Same as above
mitigation: We are applying temporary routing adjustments and adding capacity to reduce latency.
eta: 30–60 minutes for initial improvement
updated_at: <ISO8601 timestamp>"

3) Restored and RCA forthcoming:
"title: Service restored (partial restoration)
status: recovered
impact: The majority of requests in the affected region have returned to normal latency. Some customers may still see intermittent errors while we finish cleanup.
follow_up: A detailed root cause analysis and customer-impact summary will be published within 5 business days.
updated_at: <ISO8601 timestamp>"

Legal-safe external comms (customer-facing email / support reply templates):
- Principles: factual, avoid technical speculation, do not disclose internal metrics or customer data, offer mitigation steps where possible. Coordinate with Legal for any language about data exposure.

Template A — Tier 1: Brief notification (for affected customers):
"Subject: Brief update — service latency affecting text-generation in us-west-2
Hi <Customer Name>,
We detected elevated latency affecting text-generation requests in the US-West region. Our engineers are actively working on remediation and we have applied temporary routing and capacity changes to reduce impact. We will follow up with a detailed timeline and root cause analysis within 5 business days. If you are seeing degraded performance, please reply with your request IDs or reach out to your CSM.
— Redwood Inference Support"

Template B — Tier 2: Status follow-up once mitigations in progress:
"Subject: Update — mitigation in progress for text-generation latency
Hi <Customer Name>,
We wanted to share that we are applying routing changes and scaling capacity to address the latency. Initial improvements are expected within 30–60 minutes; we will notify you if that estimate changes. Please let us know if this impacts any scheduled jobs.
— Redwood Inference Support"

Template C — Post-incident customer summary (RCA-lite):
"Subject: Post-incident summary — text-generation degradation on <date>
Hi <Customer Name>,
What happened: Between <start> and <end> UTC we observed increased latency for text-generation in the US-West region affecting a subset of requests.
Impact to you: Your requests may have experienced higher latency between <window>. No customer data exposure has been detected.
Immediate mitigations: We applied routing adjustments and increased capacity which restored the majority of traffic.
Root cause: A race in autoscaling logic combined with an unanticipated model cache-growth pattern led to resource pressure on a subset of serving pools. (Detailed RCA to follow.)
Actions we’re taking: 1) Adjust autoscale thresholds and add guard rails; 2) Improve cache eviction heuristics; 3) Run targeted game day to validate fixes.
If you need further details, please reply to this message or contact your CSM.
— Redwood Inference Support"

Internal comm cadence (what to post, and when):
- Every 30 minutes while degraded: technical update to bridge with metrics and actions taken.
- Every 60 minutes to exec: 2–3 bullet summary of impact, mitigation, ETA, and customer outreach status (for incidents > 4 hours).
- After restoration: publish recovered notice and schedule RCA publication timeframe.

Game day & rehearsal guidance for sustained degradations:
- Runbook objective: validate that rotations, handoffs, and status templates work under multi-hour pressure.
- Scenario: simulate KV-cache growth + autoscaling lag causing regional latency for 6 hours.
- Success criteria: first responder handoffs occur without information loss in >90% of simulated switches; public status templates are posted within 10 minutes of bridge opening; wellbeing coordinator successfully rotates staff per policy.
- Post-game evaluation items: timeline fidelity, template clarity, rotation friction points, and any automation gaps.

Post-incident learning loop (RCA and follow-up):
1. Evidence collection within 24 hours: collect timelines, traces, logs, customer reports and the bridge transcript.
2. Draft RCA within 72 hours (RCA-lite) and publish an internal summary to the incident-postmortems folder.
3. Action items with owners and SLAs (30/60/90 days) assigned in the follow-up ticket.
4. Schedule a targeted game day within 30 days to validate mitigations if changes affect routing, autoscaling, or cache policies.

Metrics and SLO monitoring guidance (quick reference):
- Primary SLOs to watch: p95 latency per region, error rate (5xx) per route, queue depth on serving pools, KV cache hit ratio.
- Early warning thresholds (example): p95 latency increase of 20% sustained over baseline for 10 minutes; 5xx rate > 0.5% for 5 minutes.

Runbook maintenance and governance:
- Owners must review this playbook quarterly and after every sustained degradation incident.
- All changes to templates or staffing policies must be reviewed by eng-sre and customer-success before going to published state.

Appendix: checklist for bridge operator (quick):
- [ ] Create bridge and title
- [ ] Post initial Investigating status
- [ ] Capture customer-impact list and prioritize Tier 1 customers for CSM outreach
- [ ] Enforce rotation schedule and log handoffs
- [ ] Confirm legal review for any messages that mention data exposure
- [ ] Track action items and mark owners
